work.title: The Third Part of King Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 2, Scene 3
scene.title: SCENE III. A field of battle between Towton and Saxton, in Yorkshire
scene.location: A field of battle between Towton and Saxton, in Yorkshire

lines.text: Forspent with toil, as runners with a race,
lines.plainText: Forspent with toil as runners with a race

lines.text: I lay me down a little while to breathe;
lines.plainText: I lay me down a little while to breathe

lines.text: For strokes received, and many blows repaid,
lines.plainText: For strokes received and many blows repaid

lines.text: Have robbed my strong-knit sinews of their strength,
lines.plainText: Have robbed my strongknit sinews of their strength

lines.text: And spite of spite, needs must I rest awhile.
lines.plainText: And spite of spite needs must I rest awhile

lines.text: Smile, gentle heaven, or strike, ungentle death;
lines.plainText: Smile gentle heaven or strike ungentle death

lines.text: For this world frowns and Edward's sun is clouded.
lines.plainText: For this world frowns and Edward's sun is clouded

lines.text: How now, my lord, what hap? What hope of good?
lines.plainText: How now my lord what hap What hope of good

lines.text: Our hap is loss, our hope but sad despair;
lines.plainText: Our hap is loss our hope but sad despair

lines.text: Our ranks are broke and ruin follows us.
lines.plainText: Our ranks are broke and ruin follows us

lines.text: What counsel give you? Whither shall we fly?
lines.plainText: What counsel give you Whither shall we fly

lines.text: Bootless is flight, they follow us with wings;
lines.plainText: Bootless is flight they follow us with wings

lines.text: And weak we are and cannot shun pursuit.
lines.plainText: And weak we are and cannot shun pursuit

lines.text: Ah, Warwick, why hast thou withdrawn thyself?
lines.plainText: Ah Warwick why hast thou withdrawn thyself

lines.text: Thy brother's blood the thirsty earth hath drunk,
lines.plainText: Thy brother's blood the thirsty earth hath drunk

lines.text: Broached with the steely point of Clifford's lance;
lines.plainText: Broached with the steely point of Clifford's lance

lines.text: And in the very pangs of death he cried,
lines.plainText: And in the very pangs of death he cried

lines.text: Like to a dismal clangor heard from far,
lines.plainText: Like to a dismal clangor heard from far

lines.text: "Warwick, revenge! Brother, revenge my death!"
lines.plainText: Warwick revenge Brother revenge my death

lines.text: So, underneath the belly of their steeds,
lines.plainText: So underneath the belly of their steeds

lines.text: That stained their fetlocks in his smoking blood,
lines.plainText: That stained their fetlocks in his smoking blood

lines.text: The noble gentleman gave up the ghost.
lines.plainText: The noble gentleman gave up the ghost

lines.text: Then let the earth be drunken with our blood;
lines.plainText: Then let the earth be drunken with our blood

lines.text: I'll kill my horse because I will not fly.
lines.plainText: I'll kill my horse because I will not fly

lines.text: Why stand we like soft-hearted women here,
lines.plainText: Why stand we like softhearted women here

lines.text: Wailing our losses whiles the foe doth rage,
lines.plainText: Wailing our losses whiles the foe doth rage

lines.text: And look upon, as if the tragedy
lines.plainText: And look upon as if the tragedy

lines.text: Were played in jest by counterfeiting actors?
lines.plainText: Were played in jest by counterfeiting actors

lines.text: Here on my knee I vow to God above
lines.plainText: Here on my knee I vow to God above

lines.text: I'll never pause again, never stand still,
lines.plainText: I'll never pause again never stand still

lines.text: Till either death hath closed these eyes of mine,
lines.plainText: Till either death hath closed these eyes of mine

lines.text: Or Fortune given me measure of revenge.
lines.plainText: Or Fortune given me measure of revenge

lines.text: O Warwick, I do bend my knee with thine,
lines.plainText: O Warwick I do bend my knee with thine

lines.text: And in this vow do chain my soul to thine!
lines.plainText: And in this vow do chain my soul to thine

lines.text: And, ere my knee rise from the earth's cold face,
lines.plainText: And ere my knee rise from the earth's cold face

lines.text: I throw my hands, mine eyes, my heart to Thee,
lines.plainText: I throw my hands mine eyes my heart to Thee

lines.text: Thou setter up and plucker down of kings,
lines.plainText: Thou setter up and plucker down of kings

lines.text: Beseeching Thee, if with Thy will it stands
lines.plainText: Beseeching Thee if with Thy will it stands

lines.text: That to my foes this body must be prey,
lines.plainText: That to my foes this body must be prey

lines.text: Yet that Thy brazen gates of heaven may ope,
lines.plainText: Yet that Thy brazen gates of heaven may ope

lines.text: And give sweet passage to my sinful soul.
lines.plainText: And give sweet passage to my sinful soul

lines.text: Now, lords, take leave until we meet again,
lines.plainText: Now lords take leave until we meet again

lines.text: Where'er it be, in heaven or in earth.
lines.plainText: Where'er it be in heaven or in earth

lines.text: Brother, give me thy hand; and, gentle Warwick,
lines.plainText: Brother give me thy hand and gentle Warwick

lines.text: Let me embrace thee in my weary arms.
lines.plainText: Let me embrace thee in my weary arms

lines.text: I, that did never weep, now melt with woe
lines.plainText: I that did never weep now melt with woe

lines.text: That winter should cut off our spring-time so.
lines.plainText: That winter should cut off our springtime so

lines.text: Away, away! Once more, sweet lords, farewell.
lines.plainText: Away away Once more sweet lords farewell

lines.text: Yet let us all together to our troops,
lines.plainText: Yet let us all together to our troops

lines.text: And give them leave to fly that will not stay,
lines.plainText: And give them leave to fly that will not stay

lines.text: And call them pillars that will stand to us;
lines.plainText: And call them pillars that will stand to us

lines.text: And if we thrive, promise them such rewards
lines.plainText: And if we thrive promise them such rewards

lines.text: As victors wear at the Olympian games.
lines.plainText: As victors wear at the Olympian games

lines.text: This may plant courage in their quailing breasts,
lines.plainText: This may plant courage in their quailing breasts

lines.text: For yet is hope of life and victory.
lines.plainText: For yet is hope of life and victory

lines.text: Forslow no longer; make we hence amain.
lines.plainText: Forslow no longer make we hence amain
